text:
Because they bound my bones

one to another, I am.

Because someday they will unbind them,

I will no longer be.

I am and am not only through

this bit of lime and contrivance.

I walk and do not move away from a life

already made beforehand

for eternal immobility,

from a death

briefly set upright.

I still walk,

but my own death rides me:

I am the steed of my skeleton.


For one who knows how to see, shadow is only passage from light to light.


Were you unthreaded from boreal mists, or made with violet juice in a mother-of-pearl shell?...

translation.title: Because They Bound My Bones...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the skeletal paradox and also preserves the catalog's abrupt final question.
